# UML3 to database schemas: SQL DDL and NoSQL

<!-- GENERATED by tools/check_languages.py from traceability/uml3-to-languages.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Can a UML3 model be turned into a schema, and read back from one, across the engines most projects actually use? Each row is something a database expresses, how the major engines spell it, and which UML3 construct carries it. The aim is breadth of vendor coverage without breadth of language: almost every row below is a library element or a marker on an existing one, per docs/UML3-LAYERING.md, so covering another engine costs a library and not a new construct. UML3Data already models the logical and physical sides and the #mapsTo link between them; the interesting rows are the physical details a CREATE statement needs, and the ones where a document, wide-column or graph store has no relational equivalent at all.

## Coverage legend

* **COVERED**: a UML3 construct expresses it; the construct is named in the UML3 column
* **PARTIAL**: expressible, but with loss - the note says what is lost
* **GAP**: no UML3 construct expresses it; a requirement is needed if it matters
* **TBD**: not yet analyzed, or the dialect's behaviour has not been confirmed

## Targets

| Target | Version | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ISO SQL | 9075:2023 | none; analysis only |
| PostgreSQL | 17 | none; analysis only |
| MySQL | 8.4 | none; analysis only |
| SQL Server | 2022 | none; analysis only |
| Oracle | 23ai | none; analysis only |
| MongoDB | 8 | none; analysis only |
| Cassandra | 5 | none; analysis only |
| DynamoDB | - | none; analysis only |
| Neo4j | 5 | none; analysis only |

Relational columns are written against PostgreSQL 17, MySQL 8.4, Microsoft SQL Server 2022 and Oracle 23ai, and against ISO/IEC 9075:2023 where the standard settles it. Non-relational columns are written against MongoDB 8, Apache Cassandra 5, Amazon DynamoDB and Neo4j 5. No database engine is installed on this machine, so unlike the Java and Rust columns of the language map nothing here has been executed; rows whose answer depends on engine behaviour are marked TBD. An empty cell means the engine has no counterpart, which is itself information: it is why one relational shape cannot be assumed for every store.

| Schema / namespace inside a database | **PARTIAL** | metadata | `SysML package` | CREATE SCHEMA | CREATE SCHEMA | schema = database | CREATE SCHEMA | schema = user | — | — | — | — | A package groups tables, but nothing says that the package IS a SQL schema, so a generator has to assume the convention. | Unique constraint | **COVERED** | — | `UML3Data::unique` | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | unique index | — | — | uniqueness constraint | — |

## Non-relational

| Concept | Coverage | Layer | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | MongoDB | Cassandra | DynamoDB | Neo4j | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Document with a nested structure | **PARTIAL** | metadata | `UML3Data::entity`, `KerML composite feature` | — | jsonb | JSON | json | JSON | embedded document | user-defined type | map attribute | — | A composite feature already nests one entity inside another, which is the document shape. What is missing is the decision itself: nothing says whether a nested entity is embedded or stored as its own collection with a reference, and that is the central modelling choice in a document store. |
| Partition key and data distribution | **GAP** | metadata | — | — | — | — | — | — | shard key | partition key | partition key | — | Which attribute decides where a row lives determines whether a wide-column or key-value design works at all. #primaryKey says a column identifies a row, not how rows are distributed, and in Cassandra and DynamoDB the key has a partition part and a clustering part that mean different things. |
| Clustering and sort order within a partition | **GAP** | metadata | — | — | — | — | clustered index | — | — | clustering column | sort key | — | The order rows are stored in within a partition, which decides which range queries are possible at all. |
| Denormalisation for a query pattern | **GAP** | library | — | — | — | — | — | — | duplicated fields | a table per query | single-table design | — | Wide-column and key-value stores are designed backwards from the queries, so one logical entity becomes several physical tables. #mapsTo is one-to-one today and cannot express one entity realized by several tables for different access paths. |
| Consistency level and durability | **GAP** | metadata | — | isolation level | isolation level | isolation level | isolation level | isolation level | read/write concern | consistency level | strong or eventual | — | Relational isolation levels and NoSQL consistency levels are both unexpressible. This decides correctness under concurrency, and it belongs on the operation or the store rather than on the schema. |
| Time to live and expiry | **GAP** | metadata | — | — | — | — | — | — | TTL index | TTL | TTL attribute | — | Data that expires by itself has no model form, although retention is usually a compliance requirement rather than a technical one, which makes its absence more serious, not less. |
| Graph node and typed relationship | **PARTIAL** | library | `UML3Core::association`, `UML3Data::relationship` | junction table | junction table | — | graph tables | property graph | graphLookup | — | adjacency list | (a)-[:REL]->(b) | An association with ends is close to a typed relationship, and a UML3 association can carry attributes, which is what a property-graph edge is. What is missing is traversal: nothing expresses a path query, which is the whole reason to choose a graph store. |
| Schema validation in a schemaless store | **PARTIAL** | metadata | `UML3Data::entity` | — | — | — | — | — | jsonSchema validator | — | — | constraints | The model knows the shape; nothing says whether the engine should enforce it, which is a choice a document store offers and a relational one does not. |
| Key-value entry without a declared shape | **TBD** | out-of-scope | — | — | hstore | — | — | — | — | — | item | — | Redis and similar stores hold values under keys with no declared shape. Whether that is worth modelling, or is simply outside what a modelling language should claim, has not been decided - which is why the layer is out-of-scope rather than a library yet to be written. |
